Then  $w^{\prime}=f^{-1}w=f^{-1}x\cdot v_{\lambda}\in U_{q}\cdot w$ .
Furthermore, suppose  $w^{\prime}=(q-1)^{k}w^{\prime\prime}$ , with  $k>0$  and

Let  $0\neq w\in N$ . As in the proof of part (i), we can assume
that  $w\in M_{J}^{\mathbb{A}}(\lambda)$ . Using the basis of  $M_{J}^{q}(\lambda)$ , we may
write  $w=\sum u_{i}^{\prime}u_{i}\cdot v_{\lambda}$ , where  $u_{i}^{\prime}\in U_{q}^{-J}$  and  $u_{i}\in\mathfrak{n}^{q}_{-J}$  for each  $i$ . It
follows that  $\overline{u}_{i}^{\prime}\overline{u}_{i}\cdot\overline{v}_{\lambda}\neq 0$  for each  $i$.

We will assume that each $u^{\prime}_{i}$ is a monomial of type

$u_{i}^{\prime}=E_{-\beta_{i,1}+n_{i,1}\delta}^{l_{i,1}}\dots E_{-\beta_{s(i),i}+n_{s(i),i}\delta}^{l_{s(i),i}},$

where $\beta_{i,j}\in\dot{\Delta}_{+}\setminus\Delta^{J}$, and $-\beta_{i,j}+n_{i,j}\delta\neq-\beta_{k,j}+n_{k,j}\delta$ for $i\neq k$ and $u_{i}^{\prime}\neq u_{j}^{\prime}$ for $i\neq j$. Further, without loss of generality, we may also assume $w$ is homogeneous.

Then $\overline{w}=\sum\overline{u}_{i}^{\prime}\overline{u}_{i}\cdot\overline{v}_{\lambda}$ and

$\overline{u}_{i}^{\prime}=e_{-\beta_{i,1}+n_{i,1}\delta}^{l_{i,1}}\dots e_{-\beta_{s(i),i}+n_{s(i),i}\delta}^{l_{s(i),i}}.$

By [Fu5, Theorem 5.14(i)], we conclude that $\overline{u}_{i}\cdot v_{\lambda}\in\overline{N}^{f}$ for all $i$. Hence, $u_{i}\cdot v_{\lambda}$ belongs to $N_{f}^{\mathbb{A}}$, the $\mathbb{A}$ -form of $N$, and so $u_{i}\cdot v_{\lambda}$ is in $N_{f}$ for each $i$. The statement follows.     ∎

paper.title: Verma-type Modules for Quantum Affine Lie Algebras
paper.abstract: Let g be an untwisted affine Kac-Moody algebra and M_J(lambda) a Verma-type module for g with J-highest integral weight lambda. We construct quantum Verma-type modules M_J^q(lambda) over the quantum group U_q(g), investigate their properties and show that M_J^q(lambda) is a true quantum deformation of M_J(ł) in the sense that the weight structure is preserved under the deformation. We also analyze the submodule structure of quantum Verma-type modules.
